title: Arrears on a Retiree Contribution and the Ending of Group Cover under the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
1. A retiree contribution unpaid after its due day moves the enrollment into arrears on a plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans, and both the retiree and the sponsor are told.
2. Cover carries on in full throughout the grace period, and no claim is refused because a contribution is late.
3. Paying the outstanding amount in full at any time before that day ends returns the enrollment to ordinary standing with no break in cover.

## The condition on ending cover for an unpaid contribution

The contribution has been outstanding past the last day of the grace period counted from the day the plan posted the first unpaid retiree contribution charge.

The clock starts from the day the plan posted that first unpaid retiree contribution charge, taken from the posting date the plan's own records carry against that charge, and read together with the amount still outstanding on the enrollment. The plan's own records settle both, before cover is ended. The length of the period is the grace period days scheduled for the retiree's plan.

### Counting the days

Calendar days are counted from the day after that posting date, every day of the week counts, the last day of the grace period is itself inside it, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.

The day after the posting date is day one of the count. The last day of the grace period is the day whose number equals the grace period days scheduled for that plan, and, being itself inside the period, it is not a day past the period.

Two boundary readings follow. On the last day of the grace period, with the contribution still outstanding, the condition is not met. On the day after that last day, with the same contribution still outstanding, it is met.

## Where the grace period ends unpaid

Where the grace period ends unpaid, whether the enrollment ends is the sponsor's decision under its group contract, and the plan does not end cover on its own initiative.

## Where the sponsor ends the group contract entirely

Where the sponsor ends the group contract entirely, retirees get the days of notice scheduled for their plan, are told the exact date cover ends, and are told which individual plans they could move to and by when.
